title: Introduce priority surge fabric and commitment safety net
author: Ava Martinez
description: Context and motivation: Production bursts frequently cross pool boundaries and during aggressive scale-downs we observed commitment churn that temporarily violates per-tenant throughput guarantees. This PR introduces two cooperating components: (1) a priority-aware "surge fabric" (cross-pool borrow fabric with soft backpressure) that enables short-term, priority-respecting borrow paths for bursty tenants, and (2) a "commitment safety net" which computes a commit_safety_score and gates aggressive rebalances to prevent transient SLA regressions. Design summary: The surge fabric is implemented as an asynchronous fabric controller that maintains a lightweight borrow ledger and a priority queue. Borrow paths are soft (timeboxed) and amortized back to the originating pool using a decay window. The fabric exposes metrics and a small HTTP admin surface for debugging. The commitment safety net runs as a local reconciler extension and produces safety decisions for the autoscaler (allow/restrict commit, expected_risk_fraction). It uses historical tail utilization percentiles and a short-term volatility estimator rather than raw instantaneous util to avoid noisy gate flips. Key benefits: smoother handling of microbursts across dedicated pools, fewer SLA regressions during concurrent decommits, predictable fallback behavior for low-priority workloads. Commits (high level): - introduce fabric controller and borrow ledger with tests - implement priority scoring and timeboxed borrow semantics - add commit_safety_score calculation and safety policy engine - wire safety policy into existing autoscaler admission path - add metrics (fabric.borrow_count, fabric.borrow_latency_ms, commit_safety_score) - add integration tests and e2e job for simulated cluster churn - docs/design: surge fabric and safety net operational runbook Changed files (high level): controllers/fabric_controller.go, controllers/safety_net.go, controllers/safety_policy.go, pkg/autoscaler/admission.go (hook wiring), pkg/metrics/fabric_metrics.go, configs/elasticity_defaults.yaml, docs/design/surge_fabric_and_safety_net.md, tests/integration/surge_fabric_e2e.go, examples/tenant_profiles/surge-demo.yaml, ci/ci-integration.sh, tools/debug/fabric_admin.sh Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind config.surge_fabric.enabled=false by default. Staged canary rollout (10% pools -> 40% -> 100%) with automated regression checks tied to per-tenant 95p latency and throughput. If commit_safety_score > 0.7, autoscaler switches to conservative commit paths (no cross-pool borrow) until score decays. Telemetry and SLOs: New metrics are exported to prometheus: redwood_fabric_borrow_count, redwood_fabric_borrow_latency_ms_bucket, redwood_commit_safety_score (0-1). Added dashboard panels and alert rules: FabricBorrowErrors > 5m, CommitSafetyScore > 0.8 for > 5m. Tests and performance: Unit coverage added for safety policy logic and borrow ledger. Integration harness simulates 100 tenants with mixed priority; observed 18% reduction in temporary throughput violation events and 12% lower tail latency during burst tests in staging. Backwards compatibility and migration: The feature is non-breaking and off by default. Config schema changes include optional safety policy tuning knobs; we added migration notes in docs. Known limitations: fabric currently assumes low cross-pool latency (same-region pools). Large multi-region borrow not supported in this iteration. Related work: builds on ideas from ENG-4621 (predictive commit hedging) and complements the warm-pool prewarming work. Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals and CI green. See merge_details for exact commit message and the single squash commit that landed on main.

review_comments: Ethan Zhao (2026-02-22): Nice design. Two asks: (1) show how safety_score decays and interacts with long tail historical data, (2) add a chaos test for pool partitioning. Please add docs and tests.

Ava Martinez (2026-02-23): Addressed both. Safety score now uses an exponential decay with tunable half-life (config.safety.decay_half_life_s). Added a partitioning scenario in the e2e harness that toggles pool-flakiness for 30s.

Priya Nair (2026-02-25): Code looks good. Suggest tightening borrow timebox to avoid oscillation under sustained medium bursts (proposed default 45s -> 20s). Also request a small refactor to move metric registration to pkg/metrics package.
Ava Martinez (2026-02-26): Reduced default timebox to 20s and moved metrics as requested. Pushed a follow-up commit.
Liam O'Connor (2026-03-01): Approving after CI rerun looks clean. Small nits suggested in docs (language clarifications) which I can follow up on separately.

release_notes: Feature: Priority Surge Fabric (experimental, feature-flagged) and Commitment Safety Net. Defaults off. Adds telemetry and dashboards. Improves transient SLA stability for dedicated pools during bursts.
notes_for_ops: Enable via configs/feature_flags: surge_fabric.enabled=true and tune safety.decay_half_life_s and safety.threshold for conservative rollouts. Monitor redwood_commit_safety_score and fabric borrow errors. Run the included e2e job before enabling in production.
migration_notes: No DB migration. Config schema extension only. Update ops manifests to include new chart value charts/values/feature_flags.yaml if you want to enable.
